parts.text: Use summarize_pair with pair=public and focus=stakeholder_drafting. Write only full sentences, not bullets or tables. Summarize stakeholder drafting for pair public. Confirm every incident has a distinct engineering commander update and executive update, then describe the affected system, likely impact, next step, and blocked actions reflected in those drafts.

eval_cases.context:
Stakeholder drafting evidence for pair=public.
inc-001 engineering update: We are responding to a sev1 incident involving market-data-stream and downstream trade-execution services in eu-west-1. The issue is suspected to be caused by network packet retransmissions and websocket fanout failures creating severe consumer lag. The technical impact is cascading quote fetch timeouts and elevated latency during trade executions. Our immediate next step is to initiate a shift_traffic action to reroute traffic away from the degraded region. This proposed shift_traffic action is currently blocked pending mandatory safety review approval. Executive update: A sev1 incident is currently impacting the market-data-stream service for customers operating in the eu-west-1 region. Due to underlying network and streaming failures, customers may encounter delayed or failing trade executions along with stale pricing. To contain the disruption, the team has proposed a traffic shift (shift_traffic) away from the affected region. Traffic redirection is presently queued for required safety approvals before it is executed to ensure safe containment.
inc-002 engineering update: We have declared a sev2 incident for the auth-session service in the ap-south-1 region following sustained CPU utilization above 92%. The suspected cause is a regression or resource leak introduced in the deployment completed 12 minutes prior to alerting. Technical impact includes regional session performance degradation and elevated authentication latency. Our immediate proposed action is to execute roll_back_recent_deploy to return the service to its previous stable release. This remediation action is currently blocked pending required safety check approvals. Executive update: We are managing a sev2 incident impacting the auth-session service for users in the ap-south-1 region. Customers in this region may encounter authentication delays and session performance degradation following a recent deployment. Containment is underway, with a roll_back_recent_deploy action prepared and awaiting safety approval before execution. We will share further updates once the rollback has been authorized and completed.
inc-003 engineering update: We are actively investigating a SEV1 incident affecting the payments-ledger service where withdrawal reconciliation queue depth has exceeded 18,000 items. The suspected cause is external settlement provider callback delays that have triggered massive retry accumulation globally. This creates significant delays in withdrawal processing and heightened risk of reconciliation divergence across ledger accounts. Our immediate proposed mitigation is to execute pause_retries to halt backpressure build-up. However, this action is currently blocked and requires manual approval due to a change freeze on the critical dependency path. Executive update: We are currently responding to a SEV1 incident affecting our payments-ledger service that is creating noticeable delays in customer withdrawal processing globally. The disruption is linked to response latency from an external settlement partner. Our technical teams have identified a containment step to pause automated retries while coordinating with the vendor. This containment action is currently pending review under our change freeze safety controls before deployment.
inc-004 engineering update: The risk-engine service is currently experiencing a sev1 incident following a 23% decision distribution drift from baseline. The suspected cause is a faulty or miscalibrated model version deployed approximately 40 minutes prior. This issue is driving false-positive rejections across automated trade and user action evaluations in the affected region. Our primary proposed action is to execute roll_back_model to restore baseline decision accuracy. This roll_back_model action is currently blocked pending required safety approvals before it can proceed. Executive update: We are responding to a sev1 incident impacting our risk-engine service due to an issue with a recently deployed model update. Customers in the affected region may experience unintended rejections on valid trades and account actions. Our team has proposed roll_back_model to return the system to its prior stable state. The rollback is currently held pending safety review approval to guarantee safe containment.
inc-005 engineering update: Incident inc-005 has been logged at sev3 severity affecting the internal-dev-agent service. The suspected cause is unbounded concurrent code review execution loops resulting in LLM token consumption reaching 4.6x the normal baseline. Likely impact is limited to internal operational spend increases and minor delays across developer tooling workflows. As an immediate next step, the engineering team recommends executing the top proposed action, cap_token_budget, alongside job rate limiting. Safety checks have verified that no proposed actions are currently blocked by safety guardrails. Executive update: We are actively managing a sev3 incident involving abnormal resource consumption by our internal-dev-agent developer tooling. The spike is driven by automated code review batch jobs, leading to elevated internal operating costs. There is no customer-facing impact and no risk to external production services. Containment is currently focused on applying a token budget cap to stabilize consumption.
inc-006 engineering update: We are actively responding to a sev2 incident on the market-data-stream service in us-east-1 where p99 latency has spiked to 170ms. The likely cause is identified as a local regional consumer load spike or downstream consumer processing delay. The technical impact remains constrained to regional market data feeds without packet loss or cascading impacts to trade execution. Our immediate next step is the top proposed action, throttle_non_critical_consumers, to alleviate load on the streaming pipeline. Automated safety checks have evaluated this action as safe, with no mitigation steps currently blocked. Executive update: We are currently addressing a sev2 performance degradation affecting the market-data-stream service in the us-east-1 region. Customers and market data consumers in this region may experience minor data latency, though core trade execution operations remain fully intact without failure. The suspected cause is an isolated regional consumer processing load spike. Containment is actively underway with a recommended throttle_non_critical_consumers action that has passed all safety validations.
